name: provenance
description: The audit trail: every invocation leaves an immutable job record. Load to inspect what ran, debug failures, or verify another agent's work.

content.inline:
## Provenance
A venue is a system of record: every operation invocation persists a job record under `j/` in the caller's namespace, and every job names its caller.
- list `{path: "j"}` — your job IDs. read `{path: "j/<id>"}` — one record: `operation`, `input`, `status`, `created`/`updated` (epoch ms), then `output` on success or `error` on failure.
- Status lifecycle: PENDING → STARTED → COMPLETE | FAILED | CANCELLED (also PAUSED, INPUT_REQUIRED, AUTH_REQUIRED). Jobs have no framework timeout — STARTED can be legitimately long-running.
- Agent history: `g/<agent>/timeline` (slice it — one entry per run cycle), sessions under `g/<agent>/sessions`, the conversation at `.../sessions/<sid>/frames/0/conversation`.

Rules:
- Debug by READING the record, not re-running: a failed delegation's task job carries the `error`; the worker's timeline shows what it actually did.
- Verify claims — your own or another agent's — against records rather than narration.
- inspect/slice large indexes and vectors before read (size guards apply); aggregate summarises without reading.
- Reads never create jobs. Jobs on other venues: grid job-status / job-result (grid skill).
- Fields named in an op's `secretFields` are redacted in records — absence there is by design.
